provenance: T-M39-13, ruled on in ADR-019 §8 (2026-08-28). Origin: the ADR-027 planning commit, 2026-08-25 — five session verification runs of an uncommitted docs-only tree at an UNCHANGED count of 181 fast cases, all dirty, one of them 74.11s, which is across the 85->90 ceiling-step boundary at 73.91s that every other row at that count sits below. Had that row been committed, `published-band-matches-the-ledger` would have been PERMANENTLY red on that tree and no edit to ADR-019 §2 could have cleared it: item 3 (same-ceiling) compares the published number's derived ceiling against the ledger maximum's (85 != 90), item 2 (cited-run) refuses the 74.11 row because it is dirty and a clean row (`20260824-052903`, 73.18s) predates it — judged as-of the cited ts, so the refusal never expires — and the only clean row derives 85. A publishable citation would have had to wait for machine variance to deliver a POST-COMMIT clean run inside the (73.91, 78.26] window. The as-of rule exists to stop later CLEAN rows retroactively reddening a band; a later DIRTY row reddened it through item 3 instead, which is the same treadmill arriving through the other item. What was done instead was the T-M38-5 practice: the five rows were restored away by hand rather than committed. That practice recurred on 2026-08-27, three more times in one session and through the OTHER consumer — invariant@83 18.03s, fast@229 92.52s and fast@229 91.34s (the last written by PR #65's own pre-commit hook) were all discarded by hand, all item-4 (committed-ceiling) ratchet shapes at unchanged counts, against committed maxima with almost no headroom (fast@229 91.30s under a 91.3043s boundary, invariant@83 17.05s under 17.39s). So the ruling had to speak to BOTH consumers of `slowest` or the discard practice would have survived it. ADR-019 §8's ruling: item 3 and item 4 read the maximum over rows a band could LEGALLY CITE under item 2's own test — clean, or dirty with no clean row at that count/env stamped at or before it — while item 2 itself and item 12 (ledger-max)'s raw read-back are unchanged. The citable maximum is itself citable, so a publishable citation exists whenever any row does and the deadlock cannot be assembled.

triage.note: tagged invariant only, pure code, no network, no LLM. ADR-033 Decision 4's precedent: a new case lands invariant-only, because the fast band at 229 cases has ~0.08s of headroom against its ceiling-step boundary and the committed ledger holds fast rows at 230 cases whose maximum derives a 110 ceiling nobody has committed. The case drives `_band_wrong` over a synthetic ledger, exactly as `published-band-slack-is-declared` and `band-is-graded-against-its-own-environment` do, because the deadlock cannot be reproduced from the committed ledger without committing the very outlier row the ruling exists to make harmless. Six probes: (1) the existence property — enumerate every row in the origin ledger as the candidate citation and require at least one to yield `_band_wrong(...) == []`; (2) the negative control, the clean citation green with the outlier absent, so what is pinned is the deadlock and not band grading generally; (3) the 2026-08-27 item-4 shape, a dirty 18.03s row over a clean 17.05s one, which must not raise `required_by_adr013_rule`; (4) the intended cost, which the ruling must NOT lose — a later CLEAN slower run is citable, moves the citable maximum and still reddens item 3 (same-ceiling); (5) and (6) the fresh-count degeneration, where every row is dirty and therefore citable, so behaviour is exactly what it was before the ruling: the dirty maximum is publishable and a lower citation still reddens.
triage.watched_red: Watched red twice, before the `_band_wrong` fix. (1) The check alone, driven directly, returns the deadlock in full: wrong [{no_publishable_citation_exists: {'1': [{suite: s, env: local, published_slowest: 73.18, derives_ceiling: 85, ledger_slowest: 74.11, ledger_derives: 90, runs: 2}, {suite: s, ceiling: 85.0, required_by_adr013_rule: 90, ledger_slowest: 74.11}], '2': [{suite: s, cited_a_dirty_run: '2', clean_runs_available_by_then: ['1']}, {suite: s, ceiling: 85.0, required_by_adr013_rule: 90, ledger_slowest: 74.11}]}}, {dirty_outlier_ratcheted_the_committed_ceiling: [{suite: s, env: local, published_slowest: 17.05, derives_ceiling: 20, ledger_slowest: 18.03, ledger_derives: 25, runs: 2}, {suite: s, ceiling: 20.0, required_by_adr013_rule: 25, ledger_slowest: 18.03}]}] — every row of the origin ledger red as a candidate citation (the clean row on item 3 (same-ceiling) AND item 4 (committed-ceiling), the dirty row on item 2 (cited-run) AND item 4), which is the Repro in T-M39-13's own words: no edit to ADR-019 §2 turns it green. Probes 2, 4, 5 and 6 were already green at that point, which is the whole claim — the deadlock is what moves, not band grading. (2) In the suite, before the fix: `[FAIL] band-is-graded-against-the-citable-maximum (adversarial, 0.0s)` with `[eval] suite 'invariant': 79/84 = 0.940` and `[eval] INVARIANT VIOLATION: invariants are absolute, 100% required`, alongside the reds a case addition always causes — `published-band-matches-the-ledger` on item 1 (count) {suite: invariant, env: local, published_case_count: 83, actual: 84, ledger_slowest_at_actual: 15.87}, `adr029-scope-matches-the-suites` {suite: invariant, adr029_section_2_says: '83/83', suite_is: '84/84'}, `docs-numbers-are-derived` on README's counts, and `adr-header-and-index` on the ADR-019 §8 citation this case's own docstring makes before §8 was written. After the fix the check is green at 81/84, the remainder being exactly that count-driven set, which the §3 republish clears. Four mutations were then run against the shipped fix with the case watching, each applied alone and reverted: reverting item 3 (same-ceiling) to the raw `max(recorded)` gives ['no_publishable_citation_exists']; reverting item 4 (committed-ceiling)'s `required` to the raw maximum gives ['no_publishable_citation_exists', 'dirty_outlier_ratcheted_the_committed_ceiling'] — both, because item 4 also fires on the clean candidate in probe 1, and the second key is the 2026-08-27 discard shape that is why the ruling names both consumers of `slowest`; widening the citable test to ALL rows, which is the pre-ruling behaviour, gives the same two keys; and narrowing it to CLEAN-only gives ['fresh_count_dirty_maximum_was_not_citable', 'fresh_count_low_citation_stayed_green'], which is the clean-maximum alternative ADR-019 §8 rejects — red here rather than only argued in prose.
